name: Hail-Tundra
description: Hail-Tundra is a large ice world that retains a breathable atmosphere through an unusually active geological cycle of volcanic outgassing and cryogenic weathering. The surface is a vast, frozen tundra punctuated by ice mountains and methane lakes, with hailstorms that can last for weeks pelting the landscape with fist-sized spheres of compacted ice. Despite the cold, the world teems with life adapted to conditions that would be lethal to unprotected humans.

The hail is Hail-Tundra's defining characteristic, arriving in storms that build with terrifying speed and hammer the surface with concussive force. Between storms, the tundra is hauntingly beautiful, the ice plains stretching to the horizon under skies of pale lavender. The fauna are heavily armored and insulated, creatures of dense bone and thick fur that weather the hailstorms in huddled masses, their breath forming clouds that merge into the perpetual mist above the tundra.

A colonial settlement has operated here for twenty-five years, originally established as a research station but gradually growing into a permanent community of several hundred. The colonists have adapted their architecture to the hailstorms, building low, domed structures with reinforced roofs and interconnected underground passages. Their relationship with the native fauna is one of cautious coexistence, with the larger predators giving the settlement a wide berth.

Hail-Tundra's breathable atmosphere and water reserves make it one of the more habitable ice worlds, despite the punishing weather. The colony serves as a waystation for vessels operating in the outer system, and its fusion fuel reserves attract regular trade traffic. The greatest danger remains the hailstorms, which can damage ships, destroy equipment, and kill the unwary. The colonists have learned to read the sky, but newcomers still underestimate how quickly the ice can fall.
